newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Thirteen executives arrested in Vietnam fraud probe.
newsitem.headline: Thirteen executives arrested in Vietnam fraud probe.

text.p: Thirteen senior executives from Vietnam's debt-torn conglomerate Minh Phung have been arrested for suspected fraud, police in Ho Chi Minh City said on Thursday.
Directors, deputy directors and the chief accountant of the garments-to-property firm, whose boss was detained in March and subsequently charged with fraud, were all arrested on Wednesday.
There have been various reports of the debts racked up by the Ho Chi Minh City firm during a headlong expansion drive and heavy investment in a property market that has gone from boom to bust.

State Bank of Vietnam Governor Cao Si Kiem told the National Assembly two weeks ago that Minh Phung's debts, in local currency and dollars, came to around $26 million, of which about $5 million was overdue.

However, the official daily Saigon Giai Phong said director Tang Minh Phung had told investigators when he was arrested that the company's debts to banks and enterprises totalled 4.31 trillion dong ($369.6 million).

Phung was arrested on the same day as the chief executive of EPCO, a prominent trading company. Official media reports say that Minh Phung borrowed large quantities of steel and other goods from EPCO to use as collateral for a $17.1 million loan from state-owned Vietcombank.
